forms: сам, си, је, смо, сте, су; нисам; fut. бићу

examples.en: I'm a student from Novi Sad.
The weather will be nice tomorrow.

tips: The full forms јесам/јеси/јесте are used in questions (јеси ли), in a short answer («јесам»), when the verb stands alone, and for emphasis: мачак јесте био мртав - the cat really was dead.
The short yes-answer in the 3rd person is јесте (not «јест»): Да ли је то за вас? - Јесте. «Јест» survives only in the phrase «то јест» (i.e.).

note: «да» + present tense replaces the infinitive: хоћу да идем

forms: full: себе; dat. себи; instr. собом
note: «се» goes in second position in the clause, not after the verb: Ја се зовем...

examples.en: I don't know where he is.

examples.sr: [Не] брини, све ће бити у реду.
examples.en: Don't worry, everything will be fine.

note: written as one word with some verbs: нисам, немам, нећу
«у» + loc. - where; «у» + acc. - where to

forms: gen./acc. тебе, те; dat. теби, ти; instr. тобом

examples.en: I love you more than anything.

forms: gen. чега; dat. чему; var. што

examples.en: I don't know what to say.

note: «шта» - what (question); «што» - why, which
tips: The question word «what» is шта: Шта могу да кажем? Not «што могу да кажем».

note: «што пре» - as soon as possible
tips: In songs and in speech што often means «зашто» (why). So when you ask someone to repeat, don't say «што?» - a Serbian will hear "why?". Say «молим?» (pardon?).
In a question it often equals «зашто» (why): «Што си покисао?» - why are you so down? Colloquial.

forms: gen./acc. мене, ме; dat. мени, ми; instr. мном

examples.sr: [Ја̑] сам Ана, а ово је мој брат.
examples.en: I'm Ana, and this is my brother.
Wait for me in front of the building.

forms: хоћу, хоћеш; short: ћу, ћеш; нећу

examples.en: I don't want to go there.

note: ћу + infinitive = future tense: радићу, ићи ћу
tips: "They don't want to know" is «неће да знају»; «не хоће да» and «не хоћу да» are wrong. «Неће знати» means something else: they won't know (future).
«Хоћу» and «нећу» can be a reply on their own: «Назови Ивана! - Хоћу» - I will. «Нећу» means both "I don't want to" and "I won't".
The 1st person singular is хоћу, нећу (not «хоћем», «нећем»). Exceptions to the -м ending: хоћу, нећу, могу (not «можем»).

forms: gen./acc. њега, га; dat. њему, му; f. она, n. оно

examples.en: I saw him in town yesterday.

forms: gen./acc. нас; dat. нама, нам; instr. нама

examples.en: They're waiting for us at the restaurant.

note: «ми» is also the short form of «мени» (to me): дај ми

examples.en: The book is on the table.
In July we're going to the seaside.

note: мислити на + acc. - to think of someone

tips: Моћи means ability or permission: «могу да дођем сутра». Knowing facts is «знати», knowing how to do something is «умети».
The 1st person singular is могу, not «можем» (можемо is "we can"). An exception to the -м ending.
The verb is irregular: могу, можеш, може (not «можем»). Past: ја сам могао / могла.

forms: var. с; + instr. (with whom); + gen. (from where)

examples.en: I'm going to the movies with a friend.
What do you think of this idea?

tips: In speech - a hesitation pause like "uh, well": «Па не знам, овај... треба размислити». Often continued with «овај, како се зове» - "uh, what's it called".
In conversation it is often a filler word like "um, you know": «Овај... не знам шта да кажем». Not to be confused with the demonstrative "this".
In speech «овај» can also be a filler like "this, what's-it": «Дај ми нож, овај, не нож, него вилицу».

examples.en: This is a gift for you.
We were sitting at the table.

note: за + acc. of time - in: за пет минута

examples.en: Do you know where the post office is?

note: colloq. «је л'» = је ли: Је л' то истина?

examples.en: I don't know where he is.

tips: Знати is for facts and information: «знам где је продавница». A skill is «умети», possibility or permission is «моћи».

note: «имам» = I have; «има» = there is
tips: The negation is written together with the verb: «немам, немаш, нема», not «не имам». Often with the genitive: «имати среће, дара, разума».
Impersonal «има» - there is (+ gen.): «има хлеба». With time and distance: «има 80 километара», «колико година има?» - how old is he. «Имаш да радиш» - you have loads of work to do.
Има + да - must (има да ћути); има + gen. - amount, age, height (има два метра, има тридесет година); impersonal - there is (има лавова у Африци).

examples.sr: Хтео сам да дођем, [а̏ли] нисам могао.
examples.en: I wanted to come, but I couldn't.
All the children were playing outside.

forms: gen./acc. вас; dat. вама, вам; instr. вама

examples.en: We've been waiting for you for an hour.

examples.sr: Човек [ко̀јӣ] стоји тамо је мој отац.
examples.en: The man standing over there is my father.

tips: Који asks about a choice from a set: Који ауто је твој? (which of the cars); какав asks about quality: Какав је твој ауто? (what kind of car do you have).

examples.en: What do you think about it?

note: мислити на некога - to think of someone
tips: In speech the parenthetical «мислим» works like "I mean": «Не знам шта да ти кажем, мислим, нисам упућен». It is not always "I think".
мислити на + acc. - to think of someone, to have them in mind: мислим на тебе. Мислити о + loc. - to think about something: мислити о будућности. Мислити да - to think that.
«Мислити» is followed by «да» (that), not «шта» (what): «Мислим да то није добро за тебе».
It can also mean "simply": «само уради како су ти рекли» - just do as you were told.

examples.en: It's hard to say what will happen.

note: in the present tense «кажем» (from казати) is more common than «речем»
tips: Рећи has no usable present tense: "I say" is кажем (казати). The future and the past exist: рећи ћу, рекао сам. «Рекнем» is also heard in speech.

examples.en: This letter is from my mother.
I've been working here since January.
My brother is older than me.

note: in comparisons: старији од мене - older than me
«не морати» means "don't have to", not "must not"

forms: f. оне; n. она; gen./acc. њих, их; dat. њима, им

examples.en: I don't know how this is done.
What do you think about it?
I haven't seen you in years.

tips: A biaspectual verb: «видети» means both "to see" and "to catch sight of, to spot". The aspect is clear from context: «Нисам видео ниједну грешку» - I didn't spot a single mistake.

note: ићи also means "to travel": идем у Београд возом
tips: It is also used for travelling by transport: «Идем аутобусом кући», «Идете ли летос у Црну Гору?». For regular trips there is возити се.
One verb covers going, walking and travelling. Transport takes the instrumental without a preposition: ићи аутобусом, возом, колима, бициклом; on foot - ићи пешке.
«Ићи» is also used for a trip: «идемо бусом», «ишли смо авионом». Note that «дошао сам» means "I came", whether on foot, by vehicle or by plane.

examples.en: Call me if you need anything.

note: impersonal: треба ми = I need
tips: If a verb follows, use the impersonal «треба да»: «Треба да учим». If you need a thing, use personal forms: «Требају ми књиге». «Требам да учим» is heard in speech but is not standard.

examples.en: What would you like to drink?
You look like you haven't slept.

note: ради као конобар - he works as a waiter
tips: In speech it is also a marker like "sort of, like": «Ја као: хајде да свратимо на кафу». It softens a phrase or introduces someone's words, not only "as".
Colloquially «као» also means "supposedly": «Он је као болестан» - he's supposedly sick. In fast speech it shortens to «ко».
Also a filler like "like": «И она као: Мени је то много значило». «Мислим» at the start of a phrase means "I mean".

examples.en: I've lived here for five years.

tips: Besides "to work": «ради се о...» - it is about..., «не ради ми се» - I don't feel like working, «сат ради» - the clock is running, «радити домаћи» - to do homework, «на своју руку» - in one's own way.

examples.en: There were a hundred people in the hall.

note: pl. «људи»; «човече!» - colloq. address: buddy, man
tips: «Човек» means both "person" and "man". For traits of character people say особа or личност: она је оптимистична особа (not «оптимистичан човек»).
The plural comes from a different stem: «један човек - два човека, али много људи». The form «човеци» is archaic and sounds bookish or jocular.

examples.en: I have a lot of work.

note: много + gen.: много људи
tips: Before an adverb or an adjective only «много» is used: много добро, много лепо. Before a verb or a noun both «много» and «пуно» work: «хвала пуно» and «хвала много» are both fine.

examples.sr: Прво ћемо ручати, [па] ћемо у шетњу.
examples.en: First we'll have lunch, then we'll go for a walk.
She was sick, so she didn't come.

note: at the start of a phrase - "well": па добро - well, okay
tips: A conjunction: "and, then, so" (Каснили смо, па смо узели такси). Also a filler interjection "well...", often drawn out: «Па… видећемо».
In dialogue - "well": «Па, добро» - well, okay; «Па шта онда?» - so what then? Also in lists: «прво Нови Сад, па Београд, па Суботица».
When thinking or answering evasively: «Па... можда дођем» - "Well... maybe I'll come". Opening with «па» softens the reply and makes speech livelier.

examples.en: Do you want something to drink?
I have to tell you something.

examples.sr: Чекали смо [не̏што] више од сат времена.
examples.en: We waited a little more than an hour.

forms: gen./acc. кога; dat. коме; instr. ким

examples.en: Who were you with last night?
I don't know why she left.

note: нема + gen.: нема хлеба - there is no bread

examples.en: Would you like some more coffee?
I still work at the same company.

note: још увек - still

examples.en: We've been waiting in line for half an hour.
We sat in the first row.

note: у реду - all right, okay
tips: Not the color: «у реду» means "all right, okay" («Дама је у реду» - she's fine). «Ред» is also a queue, a row, a line: «чекати у реду».
«У првом реду» - first of all, «реда ради» - for form's sake, «ред вожње» - timetable, «дневни ред» - agenda, «у реду је» - fine (when paying: keep the change).

examples.en: What do you say to that?

note: in the present tense «кажем» usually replaces «речем»

tips: To avoid repeating «добар»: одличан, сјајан, диван, изврстан, савршен, фантастичан, феноменалан. To intensify, add the prefix: предобар.

examples.en: I don't know where my keys are.

examples.sr: [Ка̏д] бих имао новца, купио бих стан.
examples.en: If I had money, I would buy an apartment.

note: кад бих... - if I were to...

examples.en: The bus will arrive in ten minutes.

tips: «Дођи!» - "come here" (to children, animals). Pairs: доћи - отићи (come - leave), ући - изаћи (go in - go out).
One verb for both "come" and "arrive", by any means of travel: «Дошао сам пешке / колима» - I came on foot / by car.

note: хвала на + loc.: хвала на помоћи - thanks for the help
tips: «Хвала вама» - thank you too (in reply to thanks). «Молим» - you're welcome, «Нема на чему» - don't mention it.

examples.en: Take the keys out of the bag.
Do you want tea or coffee?

examples.sr: [И̏ли] ћеш ти доћи, или ћу ја.
examples.en: Either you'll come, or I will.
Can you give me your number?

tips: Дати гол = to score a goal. Do not confuse «гол» (goal) with «гол» (naked, f. гола).

examples.en: I'll tell you in a moment.
I have no time for that.

note: «време» is both "time" and "weather"
tips: «Колико је сати?» asks the time; «Какво је време данас?» asks about the weather. Context decides.
«Лепо време» - nice weather, «радно време» - working hours, «с времена на време» - from time to time, «у право време» - just in time.

examples.en: What are you doing? - Nothing special.

note: double negative: ништа не знам - I know nothing
tips: Also a reply to «хвала»: «Ништа!» - don't mention it. After a refusal: «Ништа, хвала» - oh well, thanks. When someone is ignored: «ти ништа» - and you said not a word.
A reply to «извините» and «хвала»: «ма ништа» (it's nothing, never mind). Not to be confused with «молим», which answers «хвала» in shops and formal settings.
«Зар» opens a question that shows surprise: «зар се нисмо упознали?» - haven't we met? «зар је тешко?» - is it that hard?

note: у ствари - in fact, actually

examples.en: I go to work every day.

note: also "second": други спрат - the second floor

examples.en: Someone is knocking at the door.

tips: Indefinite words start with «не-»: неко, нешто, негде, некад, неки. Negative ones start with «ни-» and still need «не» before the verb: «нико није дошао» - nobody came.

examples.en: I have to do it today.

note: молим - please; pardon?; you're welcome
tips: «Молити се» (with «се») - to pray: молити се Богу; without «се» - to ask: «молим те», «молити за помоћ».
«Молим» in speech: "please" and "how can I help?" (on the phone); «молим?» - "pardon?"; «молим?!» - disbelief: «Молим?! Како то мислиш?» - Excuse me?! What do you mean?

note: хајде да + present - let's...: хајде да једемо - let's eat
tips: Often without the first letter: «ајде». Used for an invitation («Ајде да идемо на кафу!»), agreement («Ајде, долазим!»), parting («Ајде, чујемо се») and "okay, fine" («Ајде, добро»).

Forms: хајде (to one person), хајдемо (we), хајдете (you, plural); also ајде, ајмо. From Turkish; the first letter is often dropped in speech. «Ајмо кући!» - let's go home. «Хајде» often nudges someone into action.

examples.en: Last year we were in Greece.

tips: «Година» is a year as a period, and also age: «Имам 35 година». Year of birth is «годиште»: «Које си годиште?» Adults are usually asked that; «Колико имаш година?» sounds like a question to a child.
«Преступна година» - leap year, «проста» - ordinary year, «берићетна» - a fruitful year (in wishes). «Година» is also a year of study at university; the plural «године» means age: «у тим годинама».

examples.en: I didn't say a single word.
There is neither bread nor milk.

note: ни ја - me neither
tips: Strengthens a negative, often like "even": «Нисам те ни питао» - I didn't even ask you. In an affirmative sentence "too" is «и»: «И ја долазим» - I'm coming too.

examples.en: We've been waiting for some time already.

tips: Means "some, a certain" and "some (people)": «неки пут» - sometimes; before a number - "about" («неких двадесет година»); as a reproach: «Баш си неки!» - you're a strange one!

examples.en: I was late because of the traffic jam.
I'll give you the money back tomorrow.
I came back from Vienna yesterday.
When will you get back home?

note: вратити се - to come back

tips: A biaspectual verb: both imperfective and perfective. Доручковати, ручати, вечерати and verbs in -овати, -исати, -ирати behave the same.
«Чуј!» opening a remark is an ironic echo of the other person: «Чуј два!» - "two, he says!"; «чуј не могу!» - "can't, you say? Of course I can!"
«Чујемо се!» - we'll be in touch, «Чуј га!» - just listen to him (ironic), «Нећу ни да га чујем» - I won't even hear of him, «Нисам добро чуо» - I didn't hear properly.

examples.en: I'm looking for a new job.
I go to work at eight.

tips: The plural «послови» means duties, operations (кућни, банкарски послови). In set phrases the plural is «посла» - affairs: «српска посла», «мешати се у туђа посла».
Stress on the first syllable: пОсао. Fleeting а: посао, посла, послу. "Where (at)?" - «на послу», "where to?" - «на посао». «На послу» is not a mistake but the locative.

note: наћи се - to meet up

examples.en: I would like to go to Paris.

note: волео бих - I would like to; љубити - to kiss

examples.en: If I'm late, Mom will kill me!
I've lived here all my life.

note: colloquially «причати» = to speak, to chat
tips: In everyday speech simply "to speak": «не прича руски» - he doesn't speak Russian, «причамо српски» - we speak Serbian.

note: declines like an adjective: његова сестра
још увек - still

examples.en: My apartment is bigger than yours.

tips: The short form (велик) comes after the verb («Јелен је велик») and for something mentioned for the first time; the long form (велики) is for a specific, already identified thing: «тај велики јелен».

examples.en: It looks like it's going to rain.

note: изгледа да... - it looks like..., it seems that...
tips: The compliment «Лепо (ми) изгледате!» - you look nice; informal: «Лепо изгледаш!». The particle «ми» adds warmth and suits a colleague, a mother-in-law, a mom.

note: хвала богу - thank God

examples.en: That's exactly what I wanted to say.

note: colloq. «баш ме брига» - I couldn't care less
tips: Besides "exactly, just" («баш сад» - right now) it often replaces «врло, јако» - "very": «Баш волим овај бенд», «Баш је топло». A colloquial intensifier.
Meanings: exactly, just («баш сад»), really, very («баш тежак дан»); in a negative sentence - "not particularly". In conversation also "really": «баш лепо» - really nice, not only "exactly".

examples.sr: Не могу да дођем [је̏р] сам болестан.
examples.en: I can't come because I'm sick.

examples.sr: Остао сам код куће [је̏р] је падала киша.
examples.en: I stayed home because it was raining.
That woman works in a bank.

examples.sr: [Зва̑о] сам те јуче, ниси се јавио.
examples.en: I called you yesterday, you didn't pick up.

note: звати - also "to phone": звао сам те - I called you
tips: "To call someone" takes the accusative: зовем Ану. The verb телефонирати, on the contrary, takes the dative: телефонирам Ани.
«Звати» - to call, to phone, to invite: «Звала ме је да би ме позвала на рођендан» - she called me to invite me to a birthday party. «Позван сам на рођендан» - I've been invited to a birthday party.
«Звати» + accusative: «зови ме» - call me, «звати на телефон». There is no separate "call back": «зваћу те касније», «звати поново».

examples.en: In my opinion, that's not true.

note: ићи по + acc. - to go and get: идем по децу - I'm going to pick up the kids

examples.en: I was sick, so I didn't come.

note: зато што - because

examples.en: It's not him who's to blame, but me.

note: не ..., већ ... - not ..., but ...
tips: Two meanings: "already" («Већ знам одговор») and "but" after a negative («Не желим кафу, већ чај»). Both can occur in one sentence: «Нисам још ручао, већ сам појео бурек».

The construction «не X, већ Y»: «Личим не на мајку, већ на бабу» - I take after my grandmother, not my mother. The negation stands before the right element or before the predicate. «Није Ана, већ Марија» - it's not Ana, but Marija. More bookish than «него».

examples.en: Wait for me in front of the cinema.
I've been waiting for you for an hour.

note: веровати + dat.: верујем ти - I believe you

examples.en: You know how much I love you.

tips: An adverb that does not change; a noun after it is in the genitive: «колико година имаш?». The adjective «колики» does decline: «колика је штета?»
Perfective: помогнем; imperative «помози!» or «помогни!»; past помогао, помогла: «Нико неће да ми помогне» - nobody wants to help me.

examples.en: That gentleman is waiting for you.

note: pl. господа: даме и господо - ladies and gentlemen

examples.en: The children are playing in the park.

note: pl. «деца» declines like a feminine singular: мала деца
tips: The plural «деца» declines like a feminine singular (gen. деце, dat. деци), but the verb and adjective are plural: «деца су мала», «децо, долазите!».
«Деца» is a collective noun with a plural verb: «деца су дошла». There is no plural «дета». With numbers: «двоје/троје деце».

examples.en: I was there two years ago.
Why didn't you say so earlier?

note: пре две године - two years ago

examples.en: You have the right to remain silent.

note: у праву си - you're right; adv. право - straight
tips: «Право» means "straight" («иди право»), not "to the right": that is «десно».
«Право» is also law as a subject («студирам право») and a legal right: «људска права» - human rights; «бити у праву» - to be right, «с којим правом» - by what right.

examples.en: What's the shortest way to the center?

note: «пут» also means "time": први пут, два пута
tips: «Пут» is a road and a journey («на путу сам» - I'm on my way) and also "time": први пут, овог пута, прошли пут, више пута, два пута, пет пута дневно, «неки други пут».
Besides "road", «пут» means "time": сваки пут - every time, овај пут - this time, први пут - the first time.
Not only "to get": добити утакмицу - to win a match; добити сина/ћерку - to have a son/daughter; добити позив - to be invited or called; «нисам те добио» - I couldn't reach you by phone.

Also: to get a shot (добити ињекцију), to win (добити на лутрији - to win the lottery), «добити корпу» - to be turned down, and to get through by phone («добили сте погрешан број» - you've dialed the wrong number).

examples.en: He drinks not tea, but coffee.

tips: Means "but" when the first part is negative: «Нисам гладна, него сам уморна». Also «него шта?» - what else!; «није само…, него и…» - not only..., but also...; in comparisons - "than".

examples.sr: [До̏к] је он радио, она је спавала.
examples.en: While he was working, she was sleeping.

note: док не + perfective verb - until

examples.en: That means a lot to me.
So, we'll see each other tomorrow?

tips: The filler «значи» is a verbal tic: «значи, ја сам...» = "so, I...". Serbs also say «па», «овај», «дакле»: much like "well", "um".
As a discourse word «значи» = "so, that is, well": «Значи, видимо се у шест.» Often just a filler in colloquial speech.

examples.en: Can you help me? - Of course!

examples.sr: Ово је моје омиљено [ме̏сто] у граду.
examples.en: This is my favorite place in the city.
In your place I wouldn't go.
I go to work every day.
Everyone has the right to make a mistake.

note: свако - everyone: свако то зна - everyone knows that

examples.en: You look a lot like your father.

note: gen. оца, voc. оче

meanings: what kind of, what sort of

examples.en: What is your new boss like?
What's the weather like in Belgrade?

note: овај - near me, тај - near you, онај - far from both
тражити од некога - to ask someone for something
tips: Besides "to look for" it means "to ask for, to demand": цариник тражи пасош - the customs officer asks for your passport. Not to be confused with питати (to ask a question).
Both "to look for" and "to ask for, to demand": тражим кључеве - I'm looking for my keys, тражим помоћ - I ask for help, тражим новац - I demand money.

examples.en: Tonight I'm sleeping at my brother's.
I'll wait for you by the post office.
Tomorrow I'm going to the doctor.

note: код куће - at home; идем код лекара - I'm going to the doctor
tips: «Код» + genitive: at a person's («идем код доктора» - I'm going to the doctor's, «код фризера сам» - I'm at the hairdresser's), or by an object («чекам те код банке»). For buildings and places use «у» and «на».
«Код куће» - at home, but «у кући» - inside the house. To people we go «код» (код лекара), to institutions «у» (у школу). Also: «код мене је кључ» - I have the key.

examples.sr: Било ми је [жа̏о] што ниси дошао.
examples.en: I was sorry that you didn't come.

note: жао ми је - I'm sorry
pl. очи is feminine: плаве очи

tips: The plural of the noun «око» is «очи» (feminine, gen. «очију»): лепе очи. The form «ока» is rarer. «Лош вид» - poor eyesight, «на левом оку» - in the left eye.
Plural: очи: плаве очи, боле ме очи. One eye - око: лево и десно око, «Боли ме десно око» - my right eye hurts.

note: used both to greet and to say goodbye

examples.en: We live in a small apartment.

note: with a preposition it splits: ни са ким - with no one
tips: Negative pronouns need a double negative: «нико није дошао», «нигде нисам био» - I haven't been anywhere.

examples.en: I asked him where he lives.

note: in speech also used as a perfective: «питао сам» - I asked

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

note: извинити се - to apologize
double negative: никад нисам... - I have never...

examples.en: We live on the second floor.

note: први спрат - the floor above the ground floor (приземље), i.e. the second floor in the US
masculine, but declines like a feminine noun: тату, тати
tips: Masculine, but declines like «мама»: «код мог тате, о мом тати». Adjectives in the plural take feminine endings: «наше тате», «нашим татама».

examples.en: How long will you stay in Belgrade?
I like to listen to music.
I don't understand what you're saying.

note: masculine: велики проблем
tips: «Проблем» is masculine, not «проблема»; plural «проблеми», gen. pl. «проблема»: «Немам проблема», «Имам проблеме».

examples.en: I lived in Russia for five years.

note: живели! - a toast: cheers!
tips: Prefixes change the meaning: преживети - to survive, to live through; оживети - to come alive; заживети - to start living, to settle in; доживети - to experience; уживети се - to settle into a place.

note: моја девојка - my girlfriend
tips: «Девојка» - a girl, a young woman and a girlfriend; «девојче» - a little girl, also an affectionate "girl"; «девојчица» - a little girl. Not to be confused with «жена» (woman, wife).

examples.en: Our house is near the sea.

note: «идем кући» - I'm going home
tips: «Кући» answers "where to": home («вратио се кући»); «код куће» answers "where": at home («код куће сам»); «кући сам» is wrong. The adjective is «кућни»: кућни љубимац - pet, кућни ред - house rules, кућне папуче - slippers.

examples.en: What did I do to you?

note: a bit more formal than «урадити»

meanings: to let in, to let through
note: пусти! - leave me alone
tips: Many meanings: to release, to let in, to put on («пусти песму»), to grow («пустити браду»), to spread a rumor, to let out paint or water. «Пусти ме» - leave me alone.
Besides "to release": to play a song, a film, cartoons: «Пусти музику!», «Пусти ми цртаће».

examples.en: I want to travel around the world.
You're the best mom in the world.
There were lots of people at the concert.
How much money do you need?

note: singular, masculine: новац је на столу - the money is on the table
tips: Singular only, neutral and fit for documents. The colloquial «паре» exists only in the plural, is a Turkish loanword, and is not used in official texts.

meanings: to be there, to be available

examples.en: They've been together for two years.
He got the job through connections.

note: нема везе - never mind, it doesn't matter
tips: Also a romantic relationship: «У вези сам» - I'm in a relationship; «љубавна веза» - a love affair. In memes «нема везе» plays on two meanings - "no connection" and "never mind".
Colloquial: «преко везе» - through connections, «немати везе» - to have no clue, «без везе» - pointless, nonsense, «нема везе» - never mind.
Also a connection as a link («телефонска, интернет веза»), a link between phenomena («веза између језика и културе») and a bunch of greens («веза першуна, младог лука»).

examples.en: Where did you leave the keys?
She left him after five years.

tips: «Момак» - a guy, a young man; also a bachelor («остати момак» - to stay single) and a boyfriend. «Дечко» - a boy, a guy; «младић» - a young man.

examples.en: I bought flowers for my mom.
I've been waiting for you for an hour.

note: колико је сати? - what time is it?
tips: «Сат» is a clock or watch (ручни, џепни сат) and an hour as a unit: «сат времена» - an hour, «сат и по» - an hour and a half. Telling time: «Колико је сати?», «у пет сати». Also a meter: «електрични сат».
«Сат» - both hour and clock (the device); a school lesson is «час». The words «сат» and «минут» are often dropped: «пола шест» - half past five, «пет до дванаест» - five to twelve.

note: declines like an adjective
осећати се - to feel (well, ill...)

examples.en: My older brother lives in Niš.

note: колико си стар? - how old are you?

examples.en: They have a son and a daughter.

note: ево - here (near me), ето - there (near you), ено - over there
tips: Ево - here (close by), ето - there (near the listener or in general), ено - over there (far): «ево је», «ето је», «ено је».
«Ево га/је/ме» - here he/she/I am: «Где ми је телефон? - Ево га». Said when showing or handing something.
With short pronouns: ево ме, ево те, ево га, ево је, ево нас, ево вас, ево их. To «Где си?» one answers «Ево ме!» - here I am.
Without «се»: «почети» means both "to begin" (something) and "to start" (by itself): «час почиње у осам». Not «почети се».
The wish is «лаку ноћ» (literally "a light night"), used for "good night".

examples.sr: Мислио сам да ћу [у̀мре̄ти] од страха.
examples.en: I thought I would die of fear.
Is it far to the center?
He lives far from the city.
Don't worry, everything will be fine.
She takes care of the children.

note: бринути о + loc. - to take care of

tips: The person it happens to is in the dative: «шта ти се десило?», «шта му се десило?» (what happened to him).

note: душо - an affectionate form of address

examples.en: It's nice to see you again.

tips: A very versatile word: «лепо се понашати» - to behave well, «лепо замолити» - to ask nicely, «лепо пише» - it's written clearly; also «хвала лепа», «молим лепо».

examples.en: I take the kids to school.
Where do you keep the keys?
Let it be as you say.
No need, thanks, I'll do it myself.

tips: «Нека» + noun - "some": «нека жена те тражи» - some woman is looking for you. «Нека» + verb - "let": «нека иде», «нека каже истину».

examples.en: I don't want to lose you.
That's not a question of money.
